/oc can we make another tweak so that whatever the current item is (so the one with the indicator) is the one that is "highlighted" when you open the dialog?

Let me summarize what I've done and verify the logic: ## Summary of Changes I modified the `DialogSelect` component in `/home/runner/work/opencode/opencode/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/ui/dialog-select.tsx` to automatically select the current item (the one with the indicator ●) when the dialog opens. ### The Change I added a new `createEffect` that: 1. Finds the index of the current item in the filtered list using `isDeepEqual(x.value, props.current)` 2. Sets the selected index to that current item's index when the filter is empty (initial state) 3. Only runs when there's no filter, so typing in search resets to first item as expected ### Key Logic ```typescript createEffect(() => { const currentIndex = flat().findIndex((x) => isDeepEqual(x.value, props.current)) if (currentIndex >= 0 && store.filter === "") { setStore("selected", currentIndex) } }) ``` This ensures that: - When the dialog opens, the current session is highlighted/selected - When the user types in the filter, it resets to the first item (existing behavior) - The current item indicator (●) remains visible as per the previous fix The change is minimal and focused, maintaining all existing functionality while adding the requested feature. I encountered this exact issue when I first packaged OpenCode for nixpkgs. The problem stems from fetching from a link which doesn't pin a specific version - whenever `api.json` gets updated on the server, you'll get a hash mismatch. In other words, the output of that `fetchContent` isn't consistent.

I solved this by packaging `models-dev` separately (see the [package definition](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/mo/models-dev/package.nix)) and then using that as a dependency.

I think I was trying to say that the UX is quite contextual to what the user is doing, and in my use case it is particularly geared towards using multiple long recurrent sessions.

So - this is a bit longer, but maybe helpful **Spoiler for attention** _the session count from opencode in the python session (see screens below) ended after 7th call with ~23,8k tokens and $0.23 costs **BUT** the real cost might differ, because of the ~235k tokens which will be invoiced by groq_ **Update:** The cost actually doesn't differ too much in my test - the dashboard shows me $0.16 for today I recently contacted groq because a session blew up to 10mio tokens (and I'm pretty sure that the session would have been 1-2mio on moonshot directly). They explained me that there might be a difference because other providers might not charge cached tokens or make it wayyy cheaper. I still had the impression something fishy is going on ... and since i love the speed of groq - and think kimi is fantastic i invested some time to track down my issue. ## TL;DR - I think that for some reason either opencode or groq add some "overhead" tokens for each request (between 10k and 30k), which because of the cached token cost of groq sooner or later get a bit expensive. - Those 10-30k might not seem a lot, but considering that opencode can work in a multi-step agentic way (f.e. calling 10 times the llm for 1 user input) - those tokens add up quickly (see my intro - 10mio) - This overhead seems smaller when calling moonshot.ai (same model) - first request for java hello world ~ 10k vs. ~ 20k - hello world in python with some text changes - ~10.4k - **Note** the session count from opencode in the python session (see screens below) ended after 7th call with ~23,8k tokens and $0.23 costs **BUT** the real cost might differ, because of the ~235k tokens which will be invoiced by groq Here are my notes from my test: ## Opencode session starts at ~11k tokens -  
  ```ts
      return [

        { name: "return", meta: true, action: "newline" },
  
  ```
  lo' and behold: I can press "alt+enter" and it makes a newline!

  ```ts
      return [
        { name: "return", action: "submit" },
        { name: "return", meta: true, action: "newline" },
        ...newlineBindings.map((binding) => ({
          name: binding.name,
          ctrl: binding.ctrl || undefined,
          meta: binding.meta || undefined,
          shift: binding.shift || undefined,
          action: "newline" as const,
        })),
        ...submitBindings.map((binding) => ({
          name: binding.name,
          ctrl: binding.ctrl || undefined,
          meta: binding.meta || undefined,
          shift: binding.shift || undefined,
          action: "submit" as const,
        })),
  ```
  What this means in my case, where I wrote this config:
  ```json
  {
    "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
    "keybinds": {
      "input_submit": "meta+return",
      "input_newline": "return"
    },
  ```
  in does **not** work.
  
  However, when I remove the two `{ name…` lines and run `bun dev`, it works:
  ```ts
      return [
        ...newlineBindings.map((binding) => ({
          name: binding.name,
          ctrl: binding.ctrl || undefined,
          meta: binding.meta || undefined,
          shift: binding.shift || undefined,
          action: "newline" as const,
        })),
        ...submitBindings.map((binding) => ({
          name: binding.name,
          ctrl: binding.ctrl || undefined,
          meta: binding.meta || undefined,
          shift: binding.shift || undefined,
          action: "submit" as const,
        })),
  ```
  Now, with my config: "return" produces a newline, "alt+return" submits!
  
  Interestingly, when I don't have my custom config and remove the two entries, with the defaults "alt+return" also **does not** work.
